h1: Fountain Tree Resort Khao Yai — An Activity-and-Farm-Village Resort Where Kids Can Play All Day on a Light Budget
intro: If your Khao Yai trip involves kids and you want a place with plenty to do on site so you don't have to drive out all day looking for things — Fountain Tree Resort Khao Yai is a name many families pick · A spacious resort in the Moo Si area of Pak Chong, its draw is 14+ adventure activities — ATV, go-kart, archery, paintball, animal feeding and a farm village — plus a cowboy zone and a swimming pool · Close to Khao Yai Farm Village · Score 7.0 from 20 reviews · From approx ฿1,800/night

body.html: What sets Fountain Tree apart from a typical Khao Yai resort is that it isn't just a place to sleep — it's a place to play · This spacious resort in Moo Si, Pak Chong leans fully into an activity-and-farm-village theme, with more than 14 adventure activities on site: ATV, go-kart, archery, paintball and laser tag, plus an animal-feeding zone (rabbits, chickens, sheep), egg collecting, candle making and mushroom picking · It's the kind of resort where kids have something to do from morning to evening without ever leaving the grounds.

There are around 60 rooms in several formats — bungalows, private villas and group shelters that sleep anywhere from 2-4 guests up to large groups of dozens · A signature touch is the cowboy-themed zone (Cowboy Town) · Rooms are practical for families and groups rather than design-led · Because the resort also hosts seminars and Walk Rally team-building, it comes with wide lawns, meeting rooms and plenty of group-activity space.

"So many activities for the kids — feeding the sheep, riding the ATV, my children loved it. Lots of space to walk around — but the rooms and fittings look dated, so set your expectations on the newness side."

There's an outdoor pool with a kids' section, BBQ facilities, and a farm village with snack stalls and a small minimart · The overall vibe is a lively activity resort that suits families with children and groups of friends more than couples after peace and quiet · It carries the SHA Extra Plus standard · One thing to understand: many activities cost extra on top of the room rate — check the packages and activity prices in advance.

To be honest per the real reviews, Fountain Tree has clear weak points · The most commonly raised issue is room condition and maintenance — the resort has been open for years, and some rooms and fittings are dated, with reviews mentioning a TV that didn't work, weak in-room Wi-Fi, and mid-level cleanliness · Some rooms come as four single beds, which may not match what some guests expect · Dining also draws criticism, with limited on-site options and an ordinary breakfast · These are things worth knowing before you book so your expectations match the price.

The location is in the Moo Si area of Pak Chong, close to Khao Yai Farm Village and Atlantis Adventure World · It sits in a zone scattered with cafes, vineyards and attractions that are an easy drive away · Worth knowing: the resort is set fairly deep off the main road, so having your own car is the most convenient option · The overall 7.0 score reflects reality — good activities and space for the money for families, but not without flaws on newness and cleanliness.

Straight up: Fountain Tree Resort Khao Yai works if you're coming as a family with kids or a group of friends, want lots of activities in one place, wide space to roam, and a light price · Kids will love the farm village, the ATV and the animal feeding — great value on the fun front · But if you're a couple expecting brand-new rooms, pretty design and a quiet boutique feel, this isn't the answer · Picturing it as a value family activity resort with its own built-in playthings is the most accurate way to see it.

A tip from reading the reviews: check the activity list and separate costs in advance, because many activities (ATV, go-kart, paintball) are charged on top of the room · If you're coming with several families or as a group, ask about combined activity-plus-stay packages for better value · Ask to see photos of the exact room type before confirming, since condition varies across bungalows, villas and shelters · And bring your own car so you can pop out to the cafes and vineyards nearby.

faqTitle: FAQ — Fountain Tree Resort Khao Yai

faq.q: Where is Fountain Tree Resort Khao Yai, and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 16 Moo 7, Nong Nam Daeng, Pak Chong, in the Moo Si area of Khao Yai · It's close to Khao Yai Farm Village and Atlantis Adventure World · About 15 minutes' drive from the Khao Yai National Park entrance · Near the Moo Si cafes and vineyards — the resort sits fairly deep off the main road, so having your own car is most convenient.

faq.q: What activities does Fountain Tree Resort Khao Yai have?
faq.a: There are 14+ adventure activities on site · ATV, go-kart, archery, paintball, laser tag, plus a farm-village and animal-feeding zone (rabbits, chickens, sheep), egg collecting, candle making and mushroom picking · Great for families with kids and groups · Many activities are charged separately from the room rate, so check the packages in advance.

faq.q: How much does Fountain Tree Resort Khao Yai cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at approximately ฿1,800/night for a Superior Bungalow · There are family rooms sleeping 4, cowboy-zone villas, and shelters for large groups · Prices vary by season — long weekends and the cool season push them up, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Fountain Tree Resort Khao Yai best for?
faq.a: It's best for families with kids and groups of friends or seminars who want lots of activities in one place, wide space and a light price · If you're a couple expecting new rooms, pretty design and a quiet boutique feel, you may need to adjust expectations, as this is a lively, long-running activity resort.

faq.q: Why do some reviews say Fountain Tree's rooms are dated?
faq.a: Because the resort has been open for years, some rooms and fittings show wear — reviews mention a TV that didn't work, weak in-room Wi-Fi and mid-level cleanliness · The upside is the abundance of activities and the light price; the trade-off is that room newness isn't a strength · Asking for photos of your room type and picking a better-condition zone helps.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: During the cool season (November–January) and long weekends, the resort hosts plenty of groups and families, so family rooms and shelters fill fast — book several weeks ahead · In normal periods, 1–2 weeks is enough · Choose a Free Cancellation option if your plans aren't firm yet.
